title: Reading Between the Lines
text:
Reading an academic article demands a different kind of attention from reading a newspaper. Readers are expected to scrutinise the methodology before accepting the findings, since a conclusion is only as reliable as the procedure behind it. Many students skip straight to the abstract, yet the discussion section often reveals the limitations the authors are willing to acknowledge.

Equally important is the way a study positions itself within existing research. A well-written article identifies a gap in the literature and explains why its hypothesis addresses that gap. Readers who notice whether results have been replicated can judge how cautiously the claims should be treated.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what must readers scrutinise before accepting the findings?
According to the second paragraph, what does a well-written article identify?
What can be inferred about students who go straight to the abstract?
options: They may miss the limitations discussed later
They always understand the study fully
They read the article in the wrong language
They prefer newspapers to academic writing

questions.text: Why would a reader check whether the results have been replicated?
options: To judge how cautiously the claims should be treated
To find the author's home address
To decide the length of the article
To choose a cover image for the article

vocabulary.definition: the system of methods used to carry out a study
a proposed explanation that a study tests
repeated by other researchers with the same result
weaknesses or restrictions that affect the findings

paragraph_translations: Czytanie artykułu naukowego wymaga innego rodzaju uwagi niż lektura gazety. Czytelnicy powinni dokładnie przeanalizować metodologię, zanim zaakceptują wyniki, ponieważ wniosek jest tak wiarygodny, jak procedura, na której się opiera. Wielu studentów pomija od razu streszczenie, a jednak sekcja dyskusji często ujawnia ograniczenia, które autorzy są gotowi przyznać.

Równie ważny jest sposób, w jaki badanie umiejscawia się wśród istniejących prac. Dobrze napisany artykuł wskazuje lukę w literaturze przedmiotu i wyjaśnia, dlaczego jego hipoteza odpowiada na tę lukę. Czytelnicy, którzy zauważają, czy wyniki zostały powtórzone, mogą ocenić, z jaką ostrożnością należy traktować stawiane tezy.
